title: ZIP: Scalable Crowd Counting via Zero-Inflated Poisson Modeling

AI.tldr: This paper proposes ZIP, a scalable crowd counting framework that models blockwise counts using a Zero-Inflated Poisson likelihood, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods across model scales on standard benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing crowd counting methods regress blockwise density maps with Mean Squared Error (MSE) losses, which dilute supervision signals due to extreme spatial sparsity (over 95% of 8x8 blocks are empty) and rely on a Gaussian error model ill-suited for discrete, non-negative count data.
AI.method: ZIP models blockwise counts with a Zero-Inflated Poisson likelihood, where a zero-inflation term learns the probability of a structurally empty block and a Poisson component models expected counts when people are present.
AI.result: Generalization analysis shows a tighter risk bound for ZIP than MSE-based losses and DMCount at moderately large training resolutions; across backbones spanning over 100x in parameters/compute, ZIP surpasses state-of-the-art methods on ShanghaiTech A & B, UCF-QNRF, and NWPU-Crowd.
AI.conclusion: Modeling crowd counts with a Zero-Inflated Poisson likelihood provides a theoretically grounded and scalable alternative to MSE regression for crowd counting.

title: Inversion-Free Style Transfer with Dual Rectified Flows

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an inversion-free style transfer framework using dual rectified flows that fuses content and style trajectories in a single forward pass.
AI.motivation: Mainstream training-free diffusion-based style transfer methods rely on computationally expensive inversion processes that reduce efficiency and introduce visual distortions when inversion is inaccurate.
AI.method: The framework predicts content and style trajectories in parallel using dual rectified flows, fuses them via dynamic midpoint interpolation that adapts to the evolving stylized image, and applies attention injection to guide style integration.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that the method generalizes across diverse styles and content images while improving visual fidelity, content preservation, and computational efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Dual rectified flows with dynamic midpoint interpolation and attention injection enable effective and efficient inversion-free style transfer.

title: Gaussian Light Field Splatting: A Physical Prior-Driven Vision Transformer for Low-Light Image Enhancement

AI.tldr: This paper proposes GLFS, a Vision Transformer for low-light image enhancement that embeds continuous 2D Gaussian Splatting light-field priors into self-attention to guide spatial gain estimation.
AI.motivation: Existing low-light image enhancement methods suffer from local exposure imbalance and color distortion under non-uniform illumination, while mainstream Vision Transformers lack explicit physics-based priors for illumination degradation.
AI.method: GLFS represents scene illumination as a superposition of anisotropic Gaussian basis functions from 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS), injects this physical bias into self-attention to infer a spatial gain field, and trains with a color vector angular loss and a luminance edge loss.
AI.result: Extensive ablation studies and quantitative evaluations show that GLFS achieves competitive overall performance in illumination correction, structure preservation, and perceptual quality.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating continuous Gaussian light field priors into Vision Transformer self-attention is an effective physical prior for low-light image enhancement.

title: On the Existential Theory of the Reals Enriched with Integer Powers of a Computable Number

AI.tldr: This paper establishes decidability and complexity bounds for the existential theory of the reals enriched with integer powers of a computable real number when its algebraicity or transcendence is known.
AI.motivation: Deciding satisfiability in the existential theory of the reals with integer powers of a computable real number r > 0 is undecidable if only a Turing machine computing r is given.
AI.method: The authors design decision algorithms for cases where r is known to be transcendental or algebraic (a root of an integer polynomial) and analyze complexity using a polynomial root barrier property.
AI.result: Under a polynomial root barrier, satisfiability is in NEXPTIME for natural numbers, EXPSPACE for algebraic numbers, and 3EXP for a family of transcendental numbers including pi and Euler's e; as a by-product, the entropic risk threshold problem for stochastic games with base e and algebraic aversion factor is shown to be in EXP without assuming Schanuel's conjecture.
AI.conclusion: Knowing the algebraicity of r circumvents undecidability in this theory and yields unconditional complexity bounds for related stochastic game problems.

title: Epidemic control under incomplete observations through mechanistic state reconstruction and multi-agent learning

AI.tldr: This paper presents a three-stage computational epidemiology framework combining observation modeling, mechanistic state reconstruction (ODE-DynNet), and multi-agent reinforcement learning for epidemic control under incomplete surveillance.
AI.motivation: Epidemic-control policies trained on raw reported infection counts suffer from suboptimal testing and isolation decisions because reporting is distorted by varying testing capacity, delays, reporting behavior, and asymptomatic infections.
AI.method: The authors extend a metapopulation SEIQR model to represent different observability regimes, propose ODE-DynNet (combining mobility-coupled epidemic dynamics with graph-temporal learning) to reconstruct hidden infection states, and optimize testing and isolation via multi-agent reinforcement learning with a flow-based responsibility-aware reward.
AI.result: On community-level mobility data from Shenzhen, China, ODE-DynNet reduces infection cost by 88% (from 4,930 to 590) compared to a non-steady partially observable decoupled policy using raw proxies without reconstruction, and remains effective across varying transmission intensities and reporting delays.
AI.conclusion: Explicit observation modeling and mechanistic state reconstruction serve as effective preprocessing steps for learned epidemic-control policies under incomplete surveillance.

title: Revisiting Mixture Policies in Entropy-Regularized Actor-Critic

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a marginalized reparameterization (MRP) gradient estimator for mixture policies in entropy-regularized actor-critic reinforcement learning, making mixture policies practical and competitive with Gaussian policies.
AI.motivation: Although mixture policies offer greater theoretical flexibility and entropy robustness than unimodal Gaussian policies in continuous action RL, standard algorithms like SAC cannot exploit them due to the lack of a low-variance reparameterization trick.
AI.method: The authors introduce the marginalized reparameterization (MRP) estimator for mixture policies and prove it has lower variance than the standard likelihood-ratio (LR) estimator in a simplified bandit setting.
AI.result: In Gym MuJoCo, MRP mixture policies significantly outperform LR counterparts; across Gym MuJoCo, DeepMind Control Suite, MetaWorld, and MyoSuite, they match or surpass Gaussian policies without retuning Gaussian-tuned hyperparameters, and clearly outperform Gaussian policies on classic-control tasks with unshaped rewards.
AI.conclusion: The marginalized reparameterization estimator resolves the high-variance gradient bottleneck of mixture policies, turning them into a practical tool for continuous control.

title: Discovery and Spatial Characterisation of Multiple Shortcut Groups for Auditing Vision Model Bias

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a per-image spatial characterization method to discover multiple recurring shortcut groups in vision models and introduces a feature intervention that reduces subgroup performance disparities.
AI.motivation: Existing attribution-based bias auditing methods aggregate regional rankings across images before computing dataset-level maps, which can mask recurring spatial shortcut patterns present only in subsets of images.
AI.method: The authors compute per-image shortcut and task contribution maps, cluster their joint representations using K-means and non-negative matrix factorization to identify shortcut groups, and propose a combined shortcut suppression and task amplification feature intervention.
AI.result: Across CelebA, CheXpert, Waterbirds, Camelyon17, and ISIC2019 on ResNet and ViT models, the discovered groups reveal shared and distinct spatial shortcut patterns linked to subgroup error rates, while input occlusion and internal interventions show that suppressing task regions degrades performance and the combined intervention generally reduces performance disparities.
AI.conclusion: Per-image spatial characterization uncovers localized shortcut groups behind subgroup errors and enables targeted feature interventions to mitigate bias.
